newsitem.title: BELGIUM: France's de Charette attacks delay in Zaire aid.
newsitem.headline: France's de Charette attacks delay in Zaire aid.

text.p: French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette criticised the international community on Monday for delaying the departure of a humanitarian aid force to Africa's Great Lakes region, hinting broadly that it could be a racial issue.
"Is it because they are African that the international community is less interested," he told reporters at a meeting of European Union foreign ministers in Brussels.
"I am frankly shocked when I see that kind of apathy hiding behind endless discussions," he said.
"It is urgent. The French position is that the international force...is more than ever necessary."
Western and African military officials who met in Stuttgart over the weekend agreed on scenarios to help feed the refugees in Zaire but there seemed no real urgency to the effort.
Support for the Canadian-led mission, authorised by the United Nations, has waned because some 600,000 Hutu refugees have returned home to Rwanda en masse since mid-November.

Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien said on Monday a force might still be needed, to help the remaining starving Rwandan refugees in eastern Zaire, but said that it could be as small as 1000-strong.
